findings.chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
findings.evidence: PDF p.96: "Time basis: this is the rate over the active business-hours window (an 8-hour × 260-workday schedule), not 24×7 wall-clock." Three lines later, the same page: "Over 24×7 the same 10 rps would extrapolate to ~18.7M requests/month on the same 260-workday calendar (10 × 3,600 × 24 × 260/12 = 18,720,000) — 3× the active-hours volume — or ~9,360 requests/user/month for 2,000 users".
findings.issue: The same quantity is labelled "not 24×7 wall-clock" and then "Over 24×7". The parenthetical arithmetic is 24 hours per *workday* on a 260-workday calendar (520 h/mo), i.e. 18.72M requests/month; a true 24×7 basis on a 730-hour month is 10 × 3,600 × 730 = 26,280,000 (~26.28M requests/month), ~40% higher. The label therefore misdescribes the basis it is attached to, in a paragraph whose whole purpose is to prevent an hour-basis mismatch — the same class of error the book flags elsewhere (e.g. the 730-hour vs 173.33-active-hour spend mismatch).
findings.fix_instruction: Rename the case to what it is — "24 hours a day on the same 260-workday calendar" (or "all wall-clock hours on workdays") — and, if a genuine 24×7 comparison is wanted, add it separately as ~26.28M requests/month (10 × 3,600 × 730).
